text:
Garry Kasparov began his chess career seriously at age seven, training at Mikhail Botvinnik's school, and quickly rose through the ranks. He won the Soviet Junior Championship in 1976 and 1977, and in 1980, became a Grandmaster. Kasparov achieved the world No. 1 ranking in January 1984, making him the youngest-ever world No. 1 player, a title he held for 12 years.
His rivalry with Anatoly Karpov was notable, culminating in the 1985–1985 match which was controversially abandoned. Kasparov won the 1985 rematch, becoming the youngest world champion at age 22. He later won the title again in 1987 and again in 1990. Following his 1986 break with FIDE, he competed under the Professional Chess Association (PCA) banner. Kasparov retired from regular competitive chess in 2005, but later continued to train players like Carlsen and Nakamura. Beyond chess, he is a prominent political dissident, heavily critical of Russian and U.S. foreign policies, and has been outspoken on issues ranging from the Israeli-Palestinian conflict to the invasion of Ukraine.
